sermon.title: Two Mothers of Revelation Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues his teaching on the harlot and the beast of Revelation 17, saying Babylon is not the Catholic Church and that the waters, nations and tongues describe a spiritual condition found in every nation. He says believing in Jesus and using his name while living your own way is spiritual fornication, explains John 8:41, and says Jesus calls his people, who are still here on earth, to come out of false religion and come to him. He closes with a Mother’s Day word to mothers and fathers about leading children well.

chunks.section_question: What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?
chunks.short_answer: He says Babylon is called a destroying mountain in Jeremiah: a nation, a group of people destroying other people for all the evil done in Zion, which he says is the church, the people of God. He says they lead astray not just Christians but people who do not believe in Jesus, and that the shepherds in Jeremiah 50:6 lead people astray on the mountains, serving God the way they should not, so that they forget their resting place, Jesus Christ.
chunks.text: Shepherds cause my people, in Jeremiah 50:6, to go astray on the what? Mountains. And what are they doing on the mountains? Serving God the way they shouldn’t be serving. And they forget their resting place. Who is our resting place? Jesus Christ. Jeremiah 51:24: “I’m against Babylon, O destroying mountain.” [Editor’s note: the words “destroying mountain” are in Jeremiah 51:25; verse 24 speaks of the evil done in Zion.] So Babylon is referred to as a what? Destroying mountain. A nation, a group of people that are destroying other people for all the evil done in Zion. Zion is the church, the people of God, and destroying all the earth. They don’t just lead Christians astray and people who believe in Jesus astray; they lead people who don’t believe in Jesus astray. Are you there? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Who are the called, chosen and faithful with the Lamb?
chunks.short_answer: He says the ten spiritual horns make war with the Lamb for one hour, and the Lamb defeats them with those who are called, chosen and faithful. He says that is us: Jesus called us to himself, he chose us when we accepted his sacrifice, and we are faithful when we keep pursuing him and living a lifestyle that pleases him.
chunks.text:
There’s ten horns are going to be ten kings for one hour with the beast. Now, obviously, these are ten spiritual horns, and for one hour they’re going to make war with the Lamb. And the Lamb is going to defeat him. And he has some people following with him, and defeats him with him, and they are called “chosen and what? Faithful.” “With him are those called, chosen, and faithful.” Didn’t Jesus call us to himself?

Yes. And when we accepted his sacrifice on the cross for our sins, admitted we were sinners and accepted forgiveness and deliverance from our sins because of him, did he choose us? Yes. And when we follow up and we pursue him and learn of him and keep living a lifestyle, we keep growing in a lifestyle pleasing him, isn’t that being faithful? Yeah, that’s us. So if that’s true, we’re still here.

chunks.section_question: Will Christians be taken out of the earth before the difficult times?
chunks.short_answer: He says the theory has Christians going out of this earth before these events, but he says he has shown in every chapter that we are still here. He says a God who could only forgive sins but could not keep us when difficult times come would be worthless, and a powerful God can also deliver us from the influence and control of sin.
chunks.text: I’m just letting it sink in. You see, the theory has got us going out of this earth before all this happens. But I’ve showed you in every chapter where we’re still here. And it makes sense. Jesus can only save us and forgive us of sins, and he cannot keep us when the difficult times come? What kind of God is that? He’s a worthless God. A powerful God can not only save us from hell and forgive us for sins, he can deliver us from the influence and control of sin. That is a God that’s got some worth, amen. And Revelation shows us that God has got a people that show in their lifestyle and serving him his power.

chunks.section_question: What do the waters in Revelation 17 mean, and is it about the United Nations or Europe?
chunks.short_answer: He says the waters where the harlot sits are people, multitudes, nations and tongues, so trying to match the beast to the United Nations or a group of European nations misses it. He says this beast is in every nation, about 190 of them, and that God has no prejudice or preference toward any nation.
chunks.text:
Now listen to this. The waters where the [unclear] sits are what? People, multitudes, nations, and tongues. So when they want to go try to get the United Nations, or, you know, the Atlantic Treaty Organization, or the ten European nations, or whatever they were that bound together over there in Europe to get the euro, their own money, and all that, they’re missing it. This beast — and this is in every nation. There is 190— approximately 190 nations. They’re in every one of them. Can I hear an amen?

But the theorists have us pondering these little packs of nations, and they always take the industrial nations. Well, you know, God loves Uganda. God loves Paraguay. God loves all these nations everywhere on the earth. He has no prejudice. He has no preference. All are the same. And every nation and every people and every language is important to him. Can I hear an amen? But they don’t make the news. It’s these bigger nations that make the news.

He calls it false religion, saying this is the right way when it is not, which is why the feminine illustration is used, and says that of the two mothers, one is really good and one is not so hot. He adds that the kingdom of God is itself a culture and a tradition we are to learn and keep.
chunks.text:
So the prophetic theorists use them. Now, there’s 6,000— over 6,000, about 6,500 languages in the earth. You see, this word tongues means languages. And so wherever there’s a language, where is this beast and this— They’re right there. You see, it is a spiritual condition that John is talking about. Can I hear an amen? It’s saying this is the right way, and it’s not. It’s saying they believe in Jesus, and they don’t believe in Jesus. It’s false religion. That’s why the woman is used. He says Jesus had all the authority but delegated the nations to Satan, a limited delegated authority.
chunks.text: All right. “The woman is the great city which rules over the kings of the earth.” Now, the Bible tells us in the garden that Jesus was tempted by Satan. And the third temptation, he came and showed him all the kingdoms of the earth and said, “Hey, these kingdoms are given to me to give to whomsoever I want. And if you’ll worship me, I’ll give you the whole earth. You’ll be the king of the earth, and all the prosperity and everything that goes with it.” Well, Satan was lying there, because Jesus is the Lord of the whole earth, and Satan cannot do anything without Jesus’s permission. chunks.short_answer: He says God cannot do evil, so any evil done in the earth is done by what the Old Testament calls the waster, whom he says God created to do what God has no character to do. He says God cannot lie and cannot reject you if you come to him, while Satan can tempt and test you, but if you follow Christ you will overcome, and there are only two roads, the wide road to hell and the narrow road to heaven.

Because — okay, did you guys hear that? Why would he give it? Because God cannot do evil. Okay? So any evil done in the earth, he created what the Old Testament calls the waster to destroy. He created Satan to do what God has no character to do.

See, there’s things God cannot do. Are you aware of that? Like, God can’t lie. Ain’t that right? God can’t reject you if you come to him. People say, “Well, God can do anything.” No, there’s things that God can’t do. Why? Because God is good. He can’t do evil. See, God can’t lie. chunks.section_question: What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?
chunks.short_answer: He says the woman used wrongly illustrates the kingdom of darkness, people who choose their own way of religion, and that we commit spiritual fornication when we follow them. He says the Jews of John 8:41 were believers who read the scriptures and had legitimate parents, but created their own way of serving God. He says Jesus told them that if God were their father they would love him, since love does no harm, and that they were harming others by leading them astray.
chunks.text:
So it’s obvious this woman and this beast is connected to which kingdom? Satan’s kingdom. The kingdom of darkness. And when we listen to these people, follow in this way, we become like them. We commit spiritual fornication. John 8:41. Now, I want to prove this to you. Here we go. You ready? I’m trying to back up that the woman used rightly is the illustration of God’s people, the church. The woman used wrongly is an illustration of the kingdom of darkness. They that choose their own way of religion, whatever it may be. These Jews were believers, isn’t that right? Here’s Jesus talking to the Jews.

They were believers. They read the scriptures. They went to the synagogue, and they talked to Jesus and say, “We’re not born of fornication.” What’s the word? Fornication. And they weren’t. They had legitimate parents. They weren’t adulterous parents. They could say that. But spiritual fornication is different. See, they created their own way of serving God. Even though they used the scriptures, even though they used God, they had their own way of doing it. And they said, “We’re not born of fornication,” but they were.

“We have one father” — who is the father? God. See, they thought they were okay. And Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would what? Love me.” See, love in the Bible would do no harm. You’d do nothing to harm me. You do nothing to harm others. You are harming others, because you’re leading them astray from me. And then he says these powerful words: “You are of your father the devil.” Because why? “The works of your father you do.”

chunks.section_question: Is it possible to believe in Jesus and still go to hell?
chunks.short_answer: He says yes: if you start using his name to worship your own way and live your own way, that is spiritual fornication, which is what the beast and the woman are about. He says it is not the Catholic, Baptist or Presbyterian church or the people who come to Christ, but anyone in them who decides to take his name and not live his way and serve him his way.
chunks.text: Are you out there? See, this is the masculine illustration, and in Revelation we have the feminine illustration. Hallelujah. So is it possible to believe in Jesus and go to hell? Yes. If you start using his name to worship your own way and live your own way, that is spiritual fornication. And that’s what this on the beast is all about. And it’s that simple. It’s not the Catholic Church. It’s not the Baptist church. It’s not the Presbyterian church or any of these people that come to Christ. It is anyone in them that decides to take his name and not live his way and serve him his way. Amen. Moms. Amen.

chunks.section_question: What does “Come out of her, my people” mean in Revelation 18?
chunks.short_answer: He says Babylon, the city that rules over the kings of the earth, has fallen and is inhabited by evil spirits, with the kingdom of darkness the main force of influence in it, and the call is to come out from this false Christianity. He says the call goes to God’s people, who are still on earth, not raptured out, and Jesus is inviting everyone to come out of their own opinions and ideas and come to him, not religion.
chunks.text:
So the [unclear] is judged. She is Babylon that rules over the kings of the earth. The mother of abominations, and martyrs and the saints. She sits on seven mountains, sits on the nations. Ten kings hate and destroy her. And Revelation 18:2, it goes on to say that Babylon, this city, this is fallen, and it’s inhabited by evil spirits. So the word fallen doesn’t mean it’s totally destroyed. It’s fallen. It’s deteriorated, and the kingdom of darkness is the main force of influence in it. Are you with me? All right. All nations, kings, merchants commit fornication with her. They’re rich through her delicacies. Here it is: “Come out from what? Her— who? The—“ Come out from this false Christianity.

Who is he saying to come out? “My people.” So where are they still? Where is the people? On earth. See, they got us in this dream world of rapturing out of here and all this bad stuff happening. But Revelation has us here handling it, because Jesus is the King of Kings and the Lord of Lords, and he is all powerful, and he keeps his people. Amen. And he’s saying, “My people, don’t have anything to do with that kind of religion.” They’re still here.

And he’s inviting everyone today to come out from your own opinions, to come out from your own ideas, to come out from your friends’ ideas and their opinions, and come to him. He’s still saying, “Come unto me, all ye that labor and heavy laden, and I will give you rest. As many as come to me, I will in no wise cast out.” Jesus is still calling out to the world through the word and through the Spirit: “Come to me,” not religion. Catholic can’t get you to heaven. Baptists can’t get you to heaven. Pentecostals can’t get you to heaven. They can’t give you wisdom and knowledge and understanding and peace and love. “I can give it all to you. Come out, my people.” And that’s what every church should be preaching: come to him. Hallelujah.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And he cried mightily with a loud voice, saying, “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and has become a dwelling place of demons, a prison for every foul spirit, and a cage for every unclean and hated bird!
And I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues.
Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
All that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out.

chunks.section_question: If I have made spiritual mistakes, can I correct them?
chunks.short_answer: He says yes: if we have made the mistake we can correct it, in the natural or in the spiritual. He says he made a lot of mistakes as a young Christian, thinking it was spiritual when it was not, and that Jesus is still the forgiver, the deliverer and the one who can save you, but you have to recognize the differences so you are not a partaker of her sins and plagues.
chunks.text: So, see, if we’ve made the mistake, can we correct it? Absolutely. In the natural, if we’re sexual immoral people or thieves and liars and so forth, can we come out and correct the natural? If in the spiritual we’re wrong, can we correct the spiritual? Yes. Thank God, I’d have been killed a long time ago, [unclear] I’ve been cast out a long time ago. I made a lot of mistakes as a young Christian, thinking it was spiritual and it wasn’t. And you can raise your hand and say, “Yeah, I can relate.” See, both in the natural and in the spiritual, he is crying, “Come to me. I’m still the forgiver. I’m still the deliverer. I’m still the one that can save you. I’m still the one that can get you to the goal.” But you got to recognize the differences to be able to make that decision, so you don’t be a partaker of her sins and of her plagues.

chunks.section_question: Why does the Bible use a mother to picture the church?
chunks.short_answer: He says it is the mother who carries, nourishes and finally gives birth to the child, while the man conceives it and gives it life. He says what the mother eats and does in the natural affects the child being born, and how she teaches it and lives before it affects it afterward, so mothers must keep the responsibility until the child is a responsible adult with good character and discipline.
chunks.text: The Bible uses the mother because it’s the mother that carries and nourishes and finally gives birth to that child. The man conceives it. He gives it life. It takes on his nature. But the mother nourishes it. And this is why the church is illustrated as a woman. See, what you eat, what you do with your body in the natural is going to affect that child being born. And after it’s born, how you teach it, the life you live before it is going to affect that child. And so, mothers, you’re very important not to just birth the child, but to keep that mother responsibility to see that that child gets to twenty years old, an adult that’s responsible, has good character, discipline in their life.

chunks.section_question: How should parents raise their children, according to this message?
chunks.short_answer: He says the woman driven into the wilderness reproduced children with great character who had the testimony of Jesus and obeyed the word of God, and that dads are included because these are spiritual decisions. He says parents should stay, support the child and the home, live as an example, and bring children to church so they see them worshiping God, and he remembers his own mother’s voice keeping him from wrong.
chunks.text:
And that’s what the woman that was driven into the wilderness had. She reproduced children with great character. They had the testimony of Jesus, and they obeyed the word of God. Wow. So, moms, have we been doing that? And can we improve on that? And dads, if you think you can escape this message, I’m going to connect you, because it says spiritually. We’re talking about spiritual decisions. And so it’s not just the woman now, but the men need to make the same decisions. Can that be an amen?

You don’t just give life to a child because you like to have sex and then just run off on it and leave it. That’s horrible. But you hang in there and you support that child. You support that home. You live an example to that home. Amen. Like Mike said, you bring them to church so they get the word of God in them from another source, not your own. Your own’s confirmed. They see you worshiping God. They don’t see you dropping them off at church and then going back home to watch the Lakers on TV or whatever. They see you right there with them. They see you are concerned about the things of God.

And see, that’s the way my mom was. And I wound up just like her. Hallelujah. And sometimes when I was a teenager and I was doing bad things, it wasn’t God bringing me under conviction; it was my mom’s voice. David, now don’t get me wrong, God used my mom’s voice to bring me in conviction. But it was my mom [unclear] that said, “Don’t you do that.” I noticed one of my older brothers was saying, “Man, mom told me three things.” And one of the things is, you know, you don’t have sex outside of marriages and have kids that you don’t raise and all that. And though he’s in his seventies, he said, “Man, if I did anything wrong, I would remember that voice.” And I said, “I’m with you. I remember that voice.”

Hallelujah. So it pays for moms to follow through on being a mom, and dads to follow through. And this morning Jesus is offering, still, for us to come out from among our own way, our own beliefs, our own religion, and embrace his

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: Does he say there are good and bad people in every church?
faqs.answer: He says he has met good Catholics, good Baptists and good Pentecostals, and lousy ones too, in the many denominations where he has ministered. He says their lifestyle and their own way of serving God comes up short in those cases.

faqs.question: What does it mean to be chosen and faithful?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus called us to himself, and when we accepted his sacrifice, admitted we were sinners and accepted forgiveness and deliverance, he chose us. He says that when we pursue him, learn of him and keep growing in a lifestyle pleasing him, that is being faithful.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “The ten horns which you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority for one hour as kings with the beast. These are of one mind, and they will give their power and authority to the beast. These will make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with Him are called, chosen, and faithful.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the theory that Christians leave the earth first?
faqs.answer: He says the theory has us going out of the earth before all this happens, but in every chapter he has shown that we are still here. He says Revelation has Jesus keeping his people here, handling it, because he is the King of Kings and Lord of Lords and is all powerful.

faqs.question: Does God love every nation equally?
faqs.answer: He says God loves Uganda and Paraguay and all the nations everywhere on the earth, and has no prejudice and no preference. He says every nation, people and language is important to him, even though the smaller ones do not make the news.

faqs.question: How many languages does he say there are?
faqs.answer: He says there are over 6,000, about 6,500 languages in the earth, and that wherever there is a language this beast is right there. He ties the word tongues to languages, and says the beast is a spiritual condition.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then he said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues.

faqs.question: Is the kingdom of God a culture?
faqs.answer: He says there are as many cultures as languages, and not everything in a culture should be kept. He says the kingdom of God is a culture and a tradition, and we are to learn that and keep that tradition and culture.

faqs.question: Can God lie or turn away someone who comes to him?
faqs.answer: He says God cannot lie and cannot reject you if you come to him, because God is good and cannot do evil. He says that when we come to Christ, however big a sinner we think we are, Jesus cannot reject us, because it is not in his nature.

scriptures.text_nkjv: All that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out.

faqs.question: Does he say there are only two spiritual roads?
faqs.answer: He says there are only two spiritual kingdoms, dark and light, right and wrong, and only two roads: the wide road to hell and the narrow road to heaven. He says Satan tries to lead you away from right and Jesus tries to lead you away from wrong, and the darkness and the light are at war.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Enter by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and there are many who go in by it. Because narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life, and there are few who find it.

faqs.question: How do we commit spiritual fornication, according to this message?
faqs.answer: He says it happens when we listen to people who follow the kingdom of darkness and follow them in their way, and we become like them. He says it means choosing your own way of religion while using the scriptures and God’s name, as the Jews did when Jesus spoke with them.

scriptures.text_nkjv: You do the deeds of your father.” Then they said to Him, “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father—God.”

faqs.question: What does he say love looks like in this passage?
faqs.answer: He says love in the Bible would do no harm: you would do nothing to harm him and nothing to harm others. He says the Jews were harming others by leading them astray from Jesus, and he points to Jesus’s words that the works of your father you do.

scriptures.text_nkjv: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it.

faqs.question: Are dads included in this message to mothers?
faqs.answer: He says that if dads think they can escape this message he is going to connect them, because it says spiritually and these are spiritual decisions. He says it is not just the woman but the men who need to make the same decisions, and that you do not give life to a child and then run off and leave it.

faqs.question: What does he say about his mother’s influence on him?
faqs.answer: He says that when he was a teenager doing bad things, it was his mother’s voice he heard, and God used her voice to bring him under conviction. He says one of his older brothers, now in his seventies, said he would remember that voice if he did anything wrong, and he says he remembers it too.
